title: ONI Companion HTTP API v1 (+v1.1): non-Screen replies
description: FROZEN. Reply bodies for /api/v1 endpoints. Screen replies use screen.schema.json. See api.md for paths, auth and errors.

code.description: v1.4: unauthorized (HTTP 401, network listener only: device token missing, unknown or removed), rate_limited (429), local_only (403: a connect-management endpoint was called from the network listener), bad_code (403: pairing code wrong, expired or used). unavailable (v1.1): the mod or the running game is needed and is not there, e.g. an action while the game is in the menu. HTTP 503.

dlcInstalled.description: DLC folders found in the install.

dlcExported.description: DLC ids covered by mod export files.

dlcMissingExport.description: Installed but never exported (the user has not started a game with it). Shown to the user; never invented.

present.description: An export or live file exists.

liveFresh.description: live.json state is running and was written recently (core decides the threshold).

connect.description: v1.4, optional. Present on the loopback listener only (never sent to a paired device).

userDir.description: The ONI user folder the core reads: the Linux build, a Proton prefix, or other.

Search.description: Ranked best first: exact name, prefix, word prefix, fuzzy.

Raw.description: GET /raw/<kind>/<id>: the merged entry exactly as the core holds it, so front ends can build custom views. Shape = the matching entry def in mod-export.schema.json (Building, Element, ...) for kinds that come from the mod export; for kind codex it is {id, title, text}. Always has id, name, dlc.

ColonyReply.description: GET /colony: a Screen plus `raw`, the colony facts in the shape of mod-live.schema.json (fields the source cannot give are left out). raw.source says which source was used.

state.description: running = live file says so; menu = live file says menu; saved = data comes from a save.

Events.description: Long-poll reply. On timeout `changed` is empty and `seq` is unchanged. A client always asks again with since=<seq>.

ActionPost.description: Body of POST /actions/<id>; the id picks the variant: focus -> ActionPostFocus, v1.3: overlay_set -> ActionPostOverlaySet, tool_select -> ActionPostToolSelect, build_select -> ActionPostBuildSelect, alert_activate -> ActionPostAlertActivate, alert_dismiss -> ActionPostAlertDismiss (anyOf: activate and dismiss bodies can look alike, the path decides). Set speed is not an action: it is POST /controls.

ActionPostAlertActivate.description: v1.2. Do what a click on the alert (or one of its highlighted lines) does in the game. 404 not_found when the core no longer has that alert; 503 unavailable in the menu / without the mod.

link.description: Index of one of the alert's links. Absent = the main click.

ActionPostAlertDismiss.description: v1.2. Dismiss the alert in the game. Only for alerts the Screen offered the action for (dismissable). The alert leaves the app on the next live.json; until then the core keeps it with `dismissing`.

ActionPostFocus.description: v1.1. Body of POST /actions/focus: one move of the game camera to one duplicant, once. Never a follow.

select.description: Also select the duplicant so its info panel opens. Default true.

ActionPostOverlaySet.description: v1.3. Body of POST /actions/overlay_set: switch the game to an overlay. `mode` is an export overlays[].id (a Screen button carries it), or "None" for no overlay. Tapping the active overlay's button sends "None", like the game. 400 for a mode the export does not list; 503 when the game is not running.

ActionPostToolSelect.description: v1.3. Body of POST /actions/tool_select: activate a game tool, ready to drag on the game screen. `priority` (1..9 or "emergency") sets the game's priority first; priority alone changes only the priority.

ActionPostBuildSelect.description: v1.3. Body of POST /actions/build_select: open the game's build menu on a building and pick it for placement. `materials` = one element id per material slot, in the building's slot order (the picker block adds it). The core refuses (400) a building that is not unlocked, with the reason in `message`; an unknown building is 404.

TabList.description: v1.3. Reply of GET /tabs: the app's tabs, named and ordered by the core. `path` is the endpoint (relative to /api/v1) the tab opens: a Screen for every tab except Codex, whose path is `kinds`: the front end draws the look-up (GET /kinds, /search, /list/<kind>, /entry) and the calculators (GET /tools). A front end shows exactly these tabs in this order. Colony, Resources, Buildings, Actions, Codex, Settings. Codex uses the game's own word for its encyclopedia (from the game's strings).

needsLive.description: The tab works only while the game runs (its buttons are disabled otherwise).

excludeKinds.description: Codex only: look-up kinds this tab leaves out (buildings have their own tab).

includesTools.description: Codex only: the calculators (GET /tools) are a section of this tab.

ModState.description: v1.3. Where the game mod stands, decided by the core; the Settings Screen shows it and Settings is the only page that names the mod. `state`: missing (not installed), disabled (installed, switched off in the game's mods.json for the active DLC set), no_live (enabled but no live data: the game is not running, or the mod failed), version_mismatch (the mod and this app do not fit; `compat.problem` says which is too old), ok. `steps` are plain-language instructions for this setup. `install.available` is true only when the app can copy its bundled mod into the game's mods folder and no copy exists yet (a Workshop copy also blocks it: two copies would both load).

copies.description: Which copies of the mod are in the game's mods folder.

target.description: Folder it would copy to (the first of `targets`).

targets.description: v1.4.1. Every ONI user folder's mods/Local/OniCompanionLink the install would write.

blocked.description: v1.4.1. Detected folders the install skips, with the plain-language reason (a Workshop copy, newest already there).

versions.description: v1.4.1. One row per detected ONI version (Linux, Proton), same order as the install targets.

updateBoth.description: v1.4.1. The installed mod versions differ between the folders.

coreSupportsMod.description: Mod versions this app can use.

mod.description: The installed mod's version, when known.

modRequiresCore.description: App versions the installed mod declares it works with.

ModVersion.description: v1.4.1. The mod's state in one ONI user folder (one game version). `enabled` follows the game's KMod rule for the DLC set active in that folder (null when no copy). `crashDisabled`: the game's crash screen emptied the mod's enabledForDlc and that version's Player.log has a logged error naming the mod. `workshop`: a Workshop copy is there (the app never adds a Local one).

library.description: Steam library holding the Proton prefix.

ModInstallPost.description: v1.3. Body of POST /mod/install. `confirm` must be true: the front end asks the user first (it shows `modState.install.target`); the core never writes into the game folder without it. 400 without confirm, 503 `unavailable` with the reason when install.available is false.

ModInstallReply.description: v1.3. Reply of POST /mod/install: the mod was copied. The game must be restarted (or its Mods menu used) to load it; `modState` says which steps remain.

ActionStatus.description: v1.1. Reply of GET /actions/<seq>. pending = written to the inbox, no ack yet; expired = no ack within 10 s.

Controls.description: v1.2. GET /controls and the reply of POST /controls (the state after the core accepted the command: `pending` is set until live.json confirms). `available` is false in the menu, with the mod missing, or when live.json is too old; `paused`/`speed` are then the last known values or absent.

game.description: What the game is doing now, for the header (front ends draw label + a dot in tone). A `controls` event goes out when it changes, also when the game's data goes stale (crash).

cause.description: F1. The real reason available is false (more exact than `reason`, which stays for older front ends). `menu` only when a fresh live file says menu; `mod_off` = ONI Companion Link is switched off in the running game; `mod_crashed` = mods.json shows the game turned it off after a crash.

message.description: F1. The sentence to show for `cause`, from the core (every front end shows the same words).

pending.description: The command the core sent that live.json has not confirmed yet; the front end highlights this button at once. Cleared when live.json matches or after 10 s.

asOf.description: writtenAt of the live.json the values come from.

ControlsPost.description: v1.2. Body of POST /controls; writes a set_speed command. pause / play (play = unpause, at `speed` if given, else the game's selected speed); speed = what the game's speed buttons do: select `speed` and keep the pause state. 503 unavailable when `available` is false; 400 for speed with pause, or state speed without speed.

Sync.description: v1.2. GET /sync, and the reply of POST /sync. The mod's companion/sync/status.json (mod-sync-status.schema.json) plus what only the core knows. `state` idle = nothing running (also before the first sync). `needed` is true when there is no art pack for the current game build + DLC set (reason no_pack), the build changed (new_build) or a DLC set changed (new_dlc, scope missing is enough).

canStart.description: False when the game is not running with the mod and a colony loaded; the front end then shows "Start Oxygen Not Included to sync".

cause.description: F1. The real reason available is false (more exact than `reason`, which stays for older front ends). `menu` only when a fresh live file says menu; `mod_off` = ONI Companion Link is switched off in the running game; `mod_crashed` = mods.json shows the game turned it off after a crash.

message.description: F1. The sentence to show for `cause`, from the core (every front end shows the same words).

queued.description: A sync was asked for while canStart was false; the core sends it by itself once a colony runs with the mod. Absent = nothing queued.

current.description: Display text of the item being drawn, e.g. "building: SynthWidget".

fonts.description: State of the fonts the core extracted / the mod exported.

SyncPost.description: v1.2. Body of POST /sync; writes a sync_assets command. When canStart is false the sync is queued (reply: queued true) and sent once the game can take it; {"cancel": true} drops a queued sync. A request while a sync is running returns the running Sync unchanged.

FontList.description: v1.2. GET /fonts: the fonts the core has for this game build, extracted from the user's own game (never shipped). `GET /fonts/<name>` serves the file: ttf as font/ttf, sdfAtlas image as image/png, table as application/json (errors stay JSON). Empty list = not synced yet; front ends use their fallbacks.

kind.description: ttf = a TrueType font file. sdfAtlasImage + sdfAtlasTable = the two files of one TextMeshPro SDF atlas (table schema: font-atlas.schema.json); they share `family`.

roles.description: Roles the game uses it for.

license.description: Short license note when known (SIL OFL for Economica / League Spartan).

SettingsPost.description: v1.1. Body of POST /settings. Same shape as ToolPost; unknown names are ignored. The reply is the settings Screen.

Identity.description: v1.4. GET /identity (network and loopback listener, no token). Who this service is. Labels only: the fingerprint is the real identity and is proven by the TLS certificate, not by this body.

instanceId.description: Random UUID v4, made on first start, kept until Reset identity.

name.description: adjective-animal, random, kept until Reset identity. Never the colony or a person.

fingerprint.description: SHA-256 of the DER certificate, lowercase hex.

fingerprintTag.description: First 4 hex digits of the fingerprint, uppercase, for lists ("spiffy-raccoon 7F3A").

address.description: IPv4 or IPv6 literal, or a Tailscale MagicDNS name.

display.description: 8 characters from ABCDEFGHJKMNPQRSTUVWXYZ23456789, shown with a dash. Compared without the dash, case-insensitive.

expiresAt.description: UTC. Valid 300 s from creation. Single use.

failuresLeft.description: Wrong tries left for the most-failed source; at 0 that source is blocked until the code ends.

deviceId.description: Random, made at pairing. Not the token.

label.description: Chosen by the companion device (e.g. its model name); untrusted text, shown as plain text.

lastSeen.description: UTC date-time of the last authorized request, null if none yet.

transport.description: How it paired. http = the iOS plain-HTTP choice (token readable on the LAN).

ConnectState.description: v1.4. GET /connect (loopback only). Same content as companion/pairing/state.json minus the file fields.

enabled.description: The Connect a phone switch. Default false after every install and after Reset identity.

listening.description: True while the network listener (TLS) is open.

port.description: TLS port while listening, else null.

plainHttp.description: The iOS plain-HTTP switch, default false. When true, a second plain-HTTP listener is open on plainHttpPort.

code.description: Null while the switch is off.

qrText.description: The exact text to encode in the QR code (pairing.schema.json QrPayload as compact JSON). Null while off.

plainHttpNote.description: One line for the window when a plain-HTTP device is paired or the switch is on; null otherwise.

ConnectSwitchPost.description: v1.4. Body of POST /connect/switch and POST /connect/plain-http (loopback only). Reply: ConnectState.

ClaimPost.description: v1.4. Body of POST /connect/claim (network listener, no token, rate limited): the one-time code for a device token.

code.description: With or without the dash, any case.

ClaimReply.description: v1.4. Reply of a good POST /connect/claim. The only time the token is shown; the core keeps only its SHA-256.

deviceToken.description: 32 random bytes, base64url without padding. Sent as header X-Oni-Device on every later request, only inside TLS to the pinned fingerprint.

ConnectDone.description: v1.4. Reply of DELETE /connect/devices/<deviceId>, POST /connect/code and POST /connect/reset-identity (loopback only). The new state follows as a connect event.

Planned.description: NOT IN V1. Pairing, for the Android/iOS standalone mode. Listed so lanes do not clash with the names.
